name: mechanical back and neck pain overview
title: Mechanical back and neck pain: axial pain worse with movement and better with rest, with no red flags, sorted by the structure it comes from (disc, disc herniation, facet joint, muscle, whiplash); each column gives what tells it apart, investigations and treatment, with the rule for who to image below

root.title: Axial neck or back pain, WORSE with movement, BETTER with rest: which structure?
lines: history with OLDCARS + red flags every time · mechanical pain has NO red flags
any red flag → image now: see the NON-MECHANICAL chart

groups.title: The DISC
lines: repeated loading → end-plate damage → tears in the anulus → disc loses height

groups.title: The FACET joint
lines: a synovial joint: it gets arthritis

groups.title: The MUSCLES
lines: no test proves it: investigate only to rule other things out

head: h
Discogenic pain
internal disc disruption: nucleus pushes into tears, anulus INTACT
h
Disc herniation
nucleus goes OUT through the anulus
tx: leg pain in a dermatome = radiculopathy: see the NON-MECHANICAL chart

head: h
Facet (zygapophyseal) pain
arthritis of the facet joint
pres: • WORSE with EXTENSION, eased by flexion
• neck → headache · low back: rarely past the knee
inv: facet degeneration does not match symptoms

head: h
Muscle
• acute strain or spasm
• repetitive strain
• myofascial trigger points
pres: • repetitive strain: repetitive or forceful tasks, vibration, awkward postures
• trigger point: tender when pressed, can refer pain
inv: rule out red flags; image only if concerned
tx: • relative rest, ice or heat, topicals

head: h
Whiplash associated disorder
acceleration-deceleration, e.g. car crash
pres: less often: facets > anterior longitudinal ligament > bone > cord
inv: • X-ray if fracture is a worry
tx: • MODEST physio: aggressive can worsen it

panels.title: Who to image (no red flags)
items: 6 weeks DESPITE good conservative care → X-ray can be the starting point
imaging indicated → MRI is best · CT only if MRI is contraindicated or unavailable
imaging is often normal, and disc degeneration is common in adults with NO back pain
